title: Phở Bò
subtitle: Vietnamese beef noodle soup with aromatic broth
excerpt: A clear, deeply fragrant beef broth scented with charred ginger, star anise, and cinnamon, poured over rice noodles and thinly sliced beef. Vietnam's most celebrated street food.

recipe.sourceNotes: Phở originated in northern Vietnam in the early 20th century, likely in or around Hanoi, and became the country's defining national dish. The soup is thought to have been influenced by the French pot-au-feu (the word phở may derive from feu, the French word for fire) and by Chinese beef noodle soups introduced by Chinese immigrants. The broth is the soul of the dish: a long-simmered, clear beef stock perfumed with toasted spices. The thinly sliced beef (served raw or very rare, cooked by the hot broth) is a characteristic of the northern Hanoi style; the southern Saigon style adds more toppings and a sweeter broth.

recipeTools.notes: A very large pot for the long broth.

content.text: Charring the ginger and onion under a grill before adding to the broth is not optional: this step is what gives phở its distinctive smoky, sweet character. Toast the spices in a dry pan until fragrant before wrapping in muslin or placing in a mesh bag. Skim the broth frequently for the first 30 minutes to keep it clear. The broth must be gently simmering, not boiling, throughout the long cook.

items.preparation: in one piece, for the broth
very thinly sliced, to serve raw in the bowl
dried flat rice noodles, soaked in cold water for 30 minutes

content.text: Make the broth: put the brisket in a large pot. Cover with cold water, bring to a boil, and cook for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse the brisket and pot. Return the brisket to the clean pot with 3 litres of fresh water. Add the charred onion and ginger, toasted spices, fish sauce, and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook, skimming frequently, for 3 to 3.5 hours until the brisket is very tender.
Remove the brisket and slice thinly. Strain the broth through a fine sieve and discard the solids. Taste and adjust the seasoning with fish sauce and salt.
Cook the soaked noodles in boiling water for 30 seconds to 1 minute until just tender. Drain and divide between deep bowls. Arrange sliced brisket and a few pieces of raw sirloin over the noodles.

Bring the broth back to a rolling boil. Ladle very hot broth over the noodles: the boiling broth cooks the raw sirloin in the bowl. Serve immediately with bean sprouts, spring onion, coriander, chilli, and lime on the side.
